sources_considered.why: Directly evaluates retrieval-augmented code generation across task categories, but does not isolate conceptual understanding.
Conference version of CodeRAG-Bench; not counted as an independent study.
Relevant controlled work on changing APIs, but later than the systems at issue and focused on documentation and memory conflicts.

evidence_items.explanation: CodeRAG-Bench reports retrieval benefits across several coding settings alongside retrieval and context-use failures. It does not establish whether a lack of conceptual understanding causes a smaller benefit on novel or changing tasks.

The study reports persistent outdated API use despite updated specifications, alongside improvements from documentation and reasoning strategies. It does not isolate downloaded code without conceptual understanding, and evaluates a later setting.

unresolved_gaps: No located study independently measures conceptual understanding and isolates its causal contribution to retrieval benefits.
The reviewed evidence lacks the matched familiar-versus-novel comparison required by the claim.
Changing API documentation is related to, but not identical with, downloading code in a dynamically changing environment.
